holes_found.description: P1 inserts an unsupported parenthetical 'Wuhan-region observation' alongside 'Mohe spring gravimeter, March 1997 eclipse'. The original WIN-012 detail_evidence calls it 'Mohe spring gravimeter, March 1997 eclipse' with no Wuhan reference; Part 6.14 existing prose calls it '1997 Mohe eclipse'; Part 6 prose calls it '1997 Mohe eclipse' too. The Wuhan attribution may be defensible if traced to the Wang Qian-shen et al. 1998 paper (which was the Wuhan SG analysis of the Mohe-path eclipse), but inserting it without a citation creates a terminology inconsistency between the new 2.13 subsection and the rest of our review. A defender will spot the inconsistency and use it to allege we are not careful with the historical record. Either (a) drop 'Wuhan-region observation' so the new subsection matches existing Part 6.14/WIN-012 terminology, or (b) keep it but add the Wang et al. 1998 citation that documents the Wuhan SG handling of the Mohe-path 1997 anomaly.
holes_found.recommendation: Edit P1 replacement_html_block to remove ', Wuhan-region observation' OR replace with ', as analyzed by the Wuhan SG team (Wang et al. 1998)' with a DOI/citation. Prefer option (a) for consistency unless the operator wants to upgrade Part 6.14 in parallel.

holes_found.description: P2 quotes only the '~500 km, generously ~1,000 km' Axis Mundi aperture case, computing B_south ~= 39 nT and a 1,660:1 ratio. But WIN-053 detail_evidence already runs an aperture sensitivity sweep — 500 km gives 1,660:1, 1,000 km gives 415x, 3,000 km still gives 46x — and concludes 'catastrophically self-contradictory regardless of aperture assumption.' A dome defender will say 'you picked your input number; we never specified the Axis Mundi aperture.' WIN-053 has the rebuttal in hand; P2 leaves it on the table. The new 2.14 subsection should carry the sensitivity envelope so the defender attack is preempted in the subsection itself, not buried in WIN-053's detail panel.
holes_found.recommendation: Edit P2 replacement_html_block: after the '1,660:1 mismatch' paragraph, add one sentence such as 'The conclusion is robust to aperture choice: even at 1,000 km aperture the discrepancy is ~415x and at 3,000 km it is still ~46x — the dome's curve-fit exceeds its own topology under every plausible aperture (see WIN-053 for the full sweep).'

holes_found.description: P4 promotes V13 from 2.9 to 2.1 (operator-choice-required, per analyst). The renumbering plus alias-preservation is mechanically clean. But P4 does not include any Part 2 intro modification explaining the new ordering principle ('foundation argument first because every other dome distance depends on the coordinate system V13 defines'). The current Part 2 intro frames the section as a sequence of self-contradictions in roughly topical order; flipping the foundational/derivative ordering without an intro signpost will disorient readers who have internalized the existing flow, and a defender will frame the renumbering as 'the authors keep rearranging because the case is unstable.' Either include the intro 1-2-sentence framing addition as part of P4, or split P4 into P4a (subsection promotion) and P4b (intro reframe) so the operator can decide on each independently.
holes_found.recommendation: If P4 executes, add an operation to insert one sentence into Part 2 intro: 'Subsection 2.1 (the V13 coordinate-system loop) appears first because every other Part 2 result is computed in coordinates the V13 critique shows are internally inconsistent — exposing the foundation before its consequences.' If the operator defers P4, no intro change is needed.

holes_found.description: P2 says 'Standard electromagnetism (Maxwell's equations, applied to the dome's own claimed topology) forbids the dome's own fitted curve' because 'a ring or toroidal field with continuous flux conservation produces 1/r-type decay (or 1/r^2 in spherically symmetric cases), not exponential.' This overstates: physically realizable multipole superpositions can approximate exponential decay over restricted radial ranges, and a sufficiently complex set of internal currents can mimic almost any functional form in a bounded domain. The much stronger structural failure (already in WIN-053) is the SAME-SIGN monopole-pair form of the fitted equation — B(r) = A*exp(-r_N/lambda) + C*exp(-r_S/lambda) with A,C both positive is the field of two same-signed monopoles, which Maxwell forbids in any closed-loop circuit. That is the deeper Maxwell-violation; the 1/r-vs-exponential point is weaker and gives a defender a hand-wavy escape ('our exponential is empirical, not first-principles'). Surface the same-sign-monopole-pair argument in 2.14 rather than relying on the magnitude-only attack.
holes_found.recommendation: Edit P2 replacement_html_block 'exponential form is also incompatible' paragraph: soften the 'Maxwell's equations forbid exponential decay' framing and add the same-sign-monopole-pair structural attack from WIN-053. Suggested replacement: 'Worse, the dome's fit has the algebraic form of two same-signed monopoles (both exponential terms have positive coefficients) — Maxwell's divergence-free condition forbids this in any closed magnetic circuit. The dome's equation describes a magnetic configuration that cannot exist, independent of the magnitude mismatch.'

After P1-P3 land, Part 2 hosts 15 named SC subsections while {{SELF_CONTRADICTED}}=20 (5 SCs remain on the WINs tab outside Part 2). The token resolves to 20 but the prose says 'in Part 2', creating a 15-vs-20 quiet mismatch that a careful defender can use to allege overcounting.
holes_found.recommendation: Rephrase to either 'any one of the self-contradictions documented in this review (Part 2 surfaces 15 of the {{SELF_CONTRADICTED}} total) alone falsifies the model' OR drop the 'in Part 2' scoping: 'any one of the {{SELF_CONTRADICTED}} self-contradictions documented in this review alone falsifies the model'.

holes_found.description: P1 uses 'kappa = 1.67 nT/uGal' in its TLDR. The dome's own published canonical value is 1.677 (used 18 times across our sections.json), and WIN-013/014 detail_verdict text uses 1.677 explicitly. The 0.4% precision difference is small but the new 2.13 subsection pivots on superconducting-gravimeter precision (0.01-0.1 uGal); using the more precise 1.677 throughout matches the precision-sensitive framing.
holes_found.recommendation: Edit P1 TLDR and detail to use 1.677 nT/uGal consistently (matches WIN-012 detail_evidence canonical phrasing and WIN-013/014 derivations).

stronger_arguments.description: In 2.14 (ring-magnet), the strongest single attack is the same-sign-monopole-pair algebraic form (see H5). It is a structural impossibility Maxwell forbids, not a magnitude disagreement — independent of every aperture choice. Worth being the second paragraph of 2.14 rather than the third.

In 2.13 (kappa divide-by-zero), the 'defense saves the past at the cost of the future' pivot (kappa 'off' at Membach/China but 'on' at BOU 2017 means kappa can also be 'off' at the August 2026 prediction site) is genuinely strong but only one paragraph deep. Could be promoted to the lead paragraph of the 'retreat to spatial heterogeneity' section since it is the actual forward-test consequence.

kernel_of_truth.description: The patch package correctly identifies the gap the c2 holistic raised: Part 2 named 12 subsections but data/wins.json had 20 SC verdicts (data/wins.json verdict scan: 20 Self-Contradicted entries confirmed). The proposed 15-named state is a measurable reduction of that gap (60% surfaced -> 75% surfaced per analyst arithmetic, verified). The choice of WIN-012/013/014 (kappa), WIN-053 (ring-magnet), and WIN-044 (FSF) as the three new subsections is well-justified: each represents a structurally distinct failure mode (numerical contradiction, topological contradiction, version-stability contradiction). The P0 renumber+Summary-relocate genuinely fixes a real reader-orphaning bug at Part 2 char ~39,516 (Summary header in middle of section). The P5 Tier-1-framing update honestly addresses the orphan attacks in Part 1.5/1.7/1.8/1.9 (h2 headers verified: '1.5 Aetheric Refraction: The Model's Universal Correction Factor', '1.7 The Gravity Paradox', '1.8 The Coordinate Collapse: One Fix Destroys the Map', '1.9 Differential Refraction: The Eclipse Geometry Trap' — names match P5 new_text). kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Structural correctness does not absolve content gaps. Two of the three new subsections (2.13 kappa, 2.14 ring-magnet) contain specific argumentative weaknesses that a defender can exploit at the subsection level (EXP-450-H1 Wuhan attribution, EXP-450-H2 aperture-sensitivity omission, EXP-450-H5 Maxwell-vs-exponential overstatement). If the patches land as drafted, the new subsections give back at the prose level what the restructure wins at the architectural level. The fixes are small additions or rephrasings to specific sentences inside P1/P2 — not rewrites — so the recommended action is integrate-after-revisions rather than block-and-resubmit. (NARRATE-CITE: EXP-450-HOL-HIERARCHY-c2-restructure.json:proposed_integration_patches[1]=P1, [2]=P2; WIN-053 data/wins.json:053.detail_evidence aperture-sensitivity envelope.)

deeper_analysis: EXP-450 is well-architected at the package level. The analyst has correctly identified that the 12-named-in-Part-2 vs 20-SC-in-wins-json gap is a structural problem (not a verdict-count problem), and the chosen three additions (kappa, ring-magnet, FSF) are not the cheapest three SCs to surface but the structurally most distinct three. P0 Summary relocation closes a real reader-orphaning bug. P5 tier-framing update is the lower-cost option vs the alternative restructure (moving 1.5/1.7/1.8/1.9 into a Part 1c) and the cost is honestly disclosed. P4 is correctly flagged operator-choice-required. The deferred items (HIER-PHASE2-05/06/07) are properly scoped — 05 and 06 require coordinated downstream work (callout boxes after the new framing lands; operator naming decision), 07 is mostly addressed by P0+P4 reordering. The package seams are in the new prose itself, not in the structural plan: H1 (Wuhan attribution), H2 (aperture-sensitivity omission), H5 (Maxwell-vs-exponential overstatement) are local fixes inside specific paragraphs. Recommended path: decider routes patches back to the analyst for the H1/H2/H5/H4 fixes (small wordings) and then re-pushes a clean class=verification batch through curmudgeon-verify to confirm the fixes landed before publish. Alternatively, the decider can self-apply the H1/H2/H5/H4 fixes if the wordings in this review's recommendation fields are sufficient guidance.
